Contrarian perspectives
- The 70% failure trope is overstated; better framing is distribution of outcomes: some succeed, many achieve partial/fragile value, and a minority collapse. This reframes “failure” and aligns with BCG and Gartner distributions. ([papers.ssrn.com](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm/5597250.pdf?abstractid=5597250&mirid=1&utm_source=openai))
- Frameworks per se are not the enemy; when adapted to product operating models (funding durable teams, outcome metrics, data/accountability design), they can succeed. MIT CISR cases highlight operating-model clarity as differentiator. ([cisr.mit.edu](https://cisr.mit.edu/publication/2020_0601_BuildingComponentizedOrganization_RossBeathNelson?utm_source=openai))
- Not all “failures” are governance problems; constraints include legacy systems, data quality, and genuine capability shortages; NAO and GAO evidence underscores these structural barriers. ([nao.org.uk](https://www.nao.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/digital-transformation-in-government.pdf))
